newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends firm but no news of buying.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends firm but no news of buying.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices maintained midday levels to end firm but trading was virtually zero with buyers hardly showing interest to offered rates, traders said.

At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board (MRELB) quoted market indicator price for November RSS 1 buyer at 309.5 cents ($1.24) a kg, up half cent from Wednesday. November SMR 20 buyer was unchanged at 306.
Trading also retained noon levels, offering the SMR 20 at 304-305 cents, SMR10 at 305-306, SMR 5 at 316-317, SMR L at 343, SMR CV at 361-362 and drum latex at 233-234 cents.
Dealers said prices firmed in the morning on signs of continuos rain and tighthening supply of raw materials.
"But business did not come through," said a dealer, adding that enquiries from Iran for some SMR grades ended in nought.
Consumer demand has been rather weak in the Malaysian rubber market in the last fortnight despite daily rains which have reduced tapping activities and supply of raw materials.
The INRO five-day average fell to 238.92 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Oct 16 from 238.92 on Oct 15. The daily indicator fell to 238.86 from 238.03 previously.
